boundary_rationale: Every reference in this row touches MT ch 21 and is written dual. Onset: a second strict word-event formula at web:Ezek.21.1 = oshb:Ezek.21.6 (וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר), byte-identical wording to web:Ezek.20.45 = oshb:Ezek.21.1, still a hard seam despite the repetition. Close: web:Ezek.21.5 = oshb:Ezek.21.10 (וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל בָּשָׂ֔ר כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה הוֹצֵ֥אתִי חַרְבִּ֖י מִתַּעְרָ֑הּ לֹ֥א תָשׁ֖וּב עֽוֹד), with a samekh immediately after. This close belongs to the wider recognition family, not the strict 28-verse list, because 'all flesh' intervenes between the verb and the closing clause; the same all-flesh subject already stood at the mashal's own close, web:Ezek.20.48 = oshb:Ezek.21.4 (וְרָאוּ֙ כָּל בָּשָׂ֔ר כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בִּֽעַרְתִּ֑יהָ לֹ֖א תִּכְבֶּֽה), disclosed here as a cross-row echo, not as boundary evidence for this row.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:Ezek.21.5 = oshb:Ezek.21.10 (dual; recognition-family close, wide sweep + parashah: samekh, single-witness)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Citing the close as the strict 28-verse recognition formula rather than the wider family was considered and rejected: the strict inventory list carries no ch 20/21 verse at all, and the all-flesh infix breaks the strict adjacency the 28-count requires.
literature_type_guess: the sword drawn against the land of Israel, the mashal's plain-sense twin
strong_or_hebrew_tags_used: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (web:Ezek.21.1 = oshb:Ezek.21.6)
device_notes: the recognition close is the wide recognition-family idiom (a book-wide sweep, not the strict 28-verse list, which carries no ch 20/21 verse); disclosed so the two counts are never blended.
